editorial:
Imagine spending all of high school hitting the books, only to find out the kids who partied also got into top colleges. That is the wake-up call Molly and Amy face in Booksmart. These two best friends are academic superstars who suddenly realize they missed out on all the fun. Determined to fix that, they set out to cram four years of partying into one wild night before graduation. The result is a fast, funny, and heartfelt ride that feels like a love letter to friendship and growing up.

The movie shines thanks to its two leads, who bring real warmth and sharp comic timing to every scene. The jokes land often, the pacing rarely slows, and the emotional beats feel earned rather than forced. Some side characters can feel a bit over the top, and a few gags run long, but the heart of the story keeps you invested. If you enjoy coming-of-age comedies with strong female leads, this one is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the girls crash the big graduation party. Molly finally kisses her crush Nick, but learns he is already with someone else. Amy shares a kiss with her crush Ryan, only to realize Ryan does not feel the same way. Hurt and frustrated, the two best friends get into a big fight and Amy storms off. By graduation morning, they make up, realizing their friendship matters more than any party. Amy heads to Botswana for a year while Molly goes to Yale, and they promise to stay close.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age comedies with strong female leads.
